1.
The present DAR has been filed on behalf of petitioners against respondents for grant of compensation in respect of death of Raj Kumar caused in a road traffic accident on 30.07.2017.

2. The brief facts in narrow compass, relevant and necessary for the disposal of the present petition are that on 30.07.2017 at about 11:00 PM, when deceased in his car bearing Registration MACT No.
1333/17 Sumitra Devi & Ors. Vs. Rajpal & Ors. 5 No. DL7CL4343 I10 reached at Kapashera Main Bijwasan Najafgarh Road, Near Suniny Meadows Estates Farm House, Bijwasan, New Delhi,
suddenly a vehicle bearing Registration No. HR30M6690 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle) which was coming from Kapashera side in a rash & negligent manner hit the car bearing registration no. DL7CL4343 I10 due to which, the deceased received fatal injuries and he was removed to RTRM Hospital, Jaffar Pur Kalan, New Delhi, where the doctor declared him brought dead.

9 The onus to prove this issue was conferred upon the petitioners.
In order to discharge their onus, PW2Inderjeet examined himself as PW02 who claimed to be eyewitness of the present case.
As per his statement, on 30.07.2017 at about 11.00 P.M. he saw one ALTO car bearing NO. HR30M6690 coming from Kapashera side hit one I10 Car.
The driver of Alto car was driving his car with very rash and negligent manner without obeying any traffic rules.
Due to this accident, the driver of I10 car received injuries.
The police officials had already taken his statement regarding that accident.

It is worthy to note here that during crossexamination, PW02Inderjeet denied the suggestion that he was not present at the spot or that he was not an eyewitness to the accident or that he had gone to the police merely on reading the newspaper or that he went to the police only to help the petitioners.
He also stated that the vehicle which hit the I10 car was having number HR30M6690.

It is relevant to pen down here that the crossexamination of PW2Inderjeet carried on by ld. counsel for the respondent no. 2/insurance company is not suggestive of anything which may discard the claim of the witness/petitioners.

It is also pertinent to mention that the respondent no.1/driver of aforesaid offending vehicle was the other material MACT No. 1333/17 Sumitra Devi & Ors. Vs. Rajpal &
Ors. 10 witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances,
the accident had taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry/trial and even did not bother to file reply to the present petition/application.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing Registration No. HR30M6690.

Not only this, the Respondent No. 1 namely Raj Pal (accused in the State case) has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/304A(A) IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation Sumitra Devi vs Raj Pal on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185231604/
7 carried out by it that the accident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.
Same would also point out towards rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing Registration No. HR30M6690 by respondent no. 1.

Even otherwise, while determining the negligence, reliance can be placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in 2009 ACJ 287, National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pushpa Rana wherein the Hon'ble High Court has held that in case the petitioner files the certified copy of the criminal record showing the completion of the investigation by the police or the issuance of charge sheet under section 279/304 A IPC or the certified copy of the FIR in addition to recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, these MACT No. 1333/17 Sumitra Devi & Ors. sentences.text: It was further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

Further, in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, 2001 ACJ 421 SC, it was held that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident is of secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injuries or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under section 166 and 140 of the Act.

sentences.text: It is also settled law that the term rashness and negligence has to be construed lightly while making a decision on a petition for claim for the same as compared to the word rashness and negligence as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in the Motor Vehicle Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

16. This aspect has also been considered by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vd. Smt. Rinki @ Rinku & Ors in MAC App. No. 200/2012 decided on 23/07/2012.

Vs. Rajpal & Ors.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry/trial and even did not bother to file reply to the present petition/application.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing Registration No. HR30M6690.
Not only this, the Respondent No. 1 namely Raj Pal (accused in the State case) has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/304A(A) IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation Sumitra Devi vs Raj Pal on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185231604/
7 carried out by it that the accident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.
This is because the chapter in the Motor Vehicle Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
It is also true that the proceedings for grant of compensation under the Act are neither governed by MACT No. 1333/17 Sumitra Devi & Ors. Vs. Rajpal & Ors. 12 the criminal procedures nor are a civil suit.
In view of abovedecision and considering facts and circumstances of the case, it stands proved that deceased Raj Kumar sustained fatal injures and died in motor accident dated 30.7.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle No. HR30M6690 which was being driven and owned by respondent no. 1Raj Pal and insured with R2/ United India Insurance Company Ltd. at the time of accident.
In light of above, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Raj Kumar died in a vehicular accident due to rash and negligent driving of the bearing No. HR30M6690 by respondent no. 1.
As per her testimony, on 30.07.20217, her husband namely Raj Kumar met with an accident and received fatal injuries and resultantly died.
In the present case, from the material and evidence on record, it is clear that Raj Kumar received fatal injuries & died in motor vehicle accident dated 30.07.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle which was being driven by R1Raj Pal.
As per the mandate of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. DTC & Anr, a multiplier of 13 is applicable for the age of 49 MACT No. 1333/17 Sumitra Devi & Ors.
Thus, petitioners will be considered dependent upon the deceased.
In these circumstances, in view of the law/guidelines laid down in the case titled as Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. DTC & Anr, being married, one Fourth (1/4th) of the income of the deceased is liable to be deducted from his total income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
13. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
In view of the above and in view of the material on record
, the annual contribution of the deceased to the family multiplied by a multiplier as per above guidelines shall give the loss of dependency to the entire family.
Further, in terms of the law /guidelines laid down MACT No. 1333/17 Sumitra Devi & Ors. Vs. Rajpal & Ors. 17 in the case  National Insurance Company Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi3, a sum of  16,500/ is awarded to the petitioners towards ' funeral expenses'.
16. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
In given fact and circumstances of the case and in view of law /guidelines laid down in the case  Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Nanu Ram and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Satinder Kaur4, a sum of  1,76,000/ ( 44,000/ x 4) is awarded as compensation under the head 'Loss of Consortium'.
